Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rbiom 4.0.0

Reproducibility

  • Every rbiom object now records how it was made. biom$history lists the constructor call and each transformation (subset(), rarefy(), mutate(), [, biom_merge(), …), and biom$code prints them as a runnable script. Direct assignments such as biom$metadata <- df are recorded as comments, since their values exist only in memory.
  • $code on tables, statistics, plots, matrices, and distance matrices is now a complete script: library calls, the object’s history, the data step, and the statistics / ggplot2 code. It is covered by tests that re-run the code in a fresh environment and compare the result to the original, including multi-panel figures, heatmaps, ordinations with taxa arrows, and data whose names contain quotes and other R syntax.
  • Data-derived strings (sample, OTU, taxa, and field names, metadata values, file paths) only ever appear in generated code as quoted literals, and rbiom never evaluates generated code itself.
  • Numbers in generated code parse back to exactly the same values on every platform: up to 15 significant digits when that is exact, and hexadecimal notation (e.g. 0x1.e999999999999p+3 for 9 * 1.7) otherwise. 17-digit decimals were read back one unit in the last place off on macOS (Apple silicon), which changed rank-based statistics.
  • $cmd no longer re-evaluates the caller’s arguments (so adiv_boxplot(rarefy(biom)) rarefies once) and no longer records cpus.
  • Functions that use random numbers (rarefy(), rank transforms with ties = "random", permutation tests, ordinations, clustering) run under seed and leave the caller’s RNG state untouched.
  • read_biom() keeps the file’s generated_by and creation date.

Statistics

  • Regression statistics with a numeric regr no longer scan ~100 positions along the x-axis for the smallest p-value (which inflated false positives to ~17%). at defaults to the median of regr, and p-values are adjusted across the whole table. Without stat.by, the reported test is the association test (the slope for lm/log; the smooth term for gam) rather than a test of “mean = 0”.
  • emtrends with stat.by now evaluates slope differences at each at position instead of averaging over them.
  • Beta diversity statistics are permutation tests on samples. bdiv_stats() and bdiv_boxplot() use PERMANOVA (adonis2), MRPP, or a dispersion test (betadisper), with pairwise PERMANOVA for bracket labels; regr and bdiv_corrplot() use a Mantel test. Wilcoxon / t-tests / regressions on pairwise distances, which treated dependent distances as independent observations, are no longer offered.
  • New strata argument for repeated-measures designs, on the *_stats(), *_boxplot(), *_corrplot(), bdiv_ord_plot(), and distmat_stats() functions. Permutation tests permute samples within strata when the tested variable varies within strata, and permute whole strata when it is constant within each stratum (exact enumeration when there are few arrangements). Regression models include a random intercept per stratum. Rank tests report an error rather than ignoring strata.
  • bdiv_ord_table() / bdiv_ord_plot() compute distances on the data as given (no hidden relativization), use stats::cmdscale() for PCoA with “% variance explained” axis labels, and test taxa biplot vectors with vegan::envfit(). p.top handles tied p-values and adjusts before filtering.
  • bdiv_clusters() uses k-medoids (cluster::pam()) on the distance matrix; taxa_clusters() uses 10 k-means starts. Both accept seed.
  • Wilcoxon tests use exact = NULL; the estimate column is now .loc.shift (Hodges-Lehmann). level is honored. Captions name the p-value adjustment method correctly.
  • When a Wilcoxon confidence interval can’t reach the requested level (very small groups), it is reported as unbounded (-Inf, Inf) on every R version, as R >= 4.6 does, rather than as a narrower interval at a lower level. On R < 4.6, the warnings about this and about falling back to the normal approximation for ties are no longer shown.
  • adiv_boxplot(), bdiv_boxplot(), and taxa_boxplot() gain a test argument.
  • Dropped rows with missing values and comparisons that could not be computed are reported in one message / warning instead of silently ignored.
  • bdiv_heatmap() clusters samples on the chosen distance metric.
  • The log transform in taxa_matrix() uses a pseudocount so absent taxa rank lowest.

Data handling

  • subset() and subset_taxa() treat NA conditions as FALSE, like base::subset().
  • Single-sample and single-OTU objects work (biom[1]).
  • biom$relative is TRUE for relative-abundance data; biom$depth is no longer reported as 1 for such data.
  • Clear errors for NA, negative, or non-numeric counts and unknown sample/OTU names. as_rbiom() accepts data frames of counts.
  • write_biom(format = "json") no longer rounds values to four decimals.
  • Newick output quotes labels containing metacharacters, spaces, or underscores, keeps node labels, and handles large trees. With ecodive 2.3.1’s standard-conforming parser, labels containing apostrophes and square brackets (e.g. o__[Saprospirales]) now round-trip exactly, and malformed Newick input is an error rather than a garbled tree.
  • read_fasta() returns a named character vector, accepts URLs and compressed files, and is linear-time.
  • tree_subset() handles unsorted numeric tips and keeps node labels.
  • biom_merge() accepts anything as_rbiom() accepts, keeps a tree that covers all OTUs, and reports conflicts in one warning.
  • Tabular imports no longer depend on readr; sample IDs like "1.10" stay character, and Body Site is never renamed to Body.Site.
  • Many fixes to TSV/HDF5 round trips (dates, column order, logical columns, blank cells), write_xlsx(), convert_to_*(), and the exec/ scripts.
  • Caching works when disabled; keys include package versions; only rbiom’s own files are ever evicted from the cache directory.

Plots

  • ggbeeswarm, ggrepel, and fillpattern are optional. Without them, dot and strip layers use jittered points and taxa labels use geom_label().
  • Arguments in ... that don’t match any layer are an error that lists the valid layer prefixes (previously they produced cryptic ggplot2 errors). b. now refers to the bar layer and box. to the box layer.
  • Fixed: flipped boxplots without x, confidence intervals clamped at zero, heatmap dendrogram placement and tree_height, single-taxon heatmaps, rare_stacked(labels = TRUE), xlab.angle, empty statistics tables, and ordination ellipses for small groups.
  • Plot titles use readable metric names.

Breaking changes

  • write_*() functions refuse to overwrite an existing file unless overwrite = TRUE. Text output uses LF line endings on all platforms.
  • The plyr functions ., ddply, ldply, and llply are no longer re-exported.
  • Removed transform = "percent" (never worked), and the never-functional apcoa and tree-plotting code.
  • bdiv = "unifrac" is now an error because it is ambiguous; name the variant (e.g. "unweighted_unifrac").
  • Statistics table columns changed as described above.

Dependencies

  • Removed: ape, crayon, ggtext, labeling, pillar, plyr, readr. Moved to Suggests: fillpattern, ggbeeswarm, ggrepel, readxl. Packages that were always required but undeclared (cli, glue, lifecycle, Matrix, R6, rlang, scales, tibble) are now in Imports, along with cluster and permute (both already installed with vegan).
  • Requires ecodive (>= 2.3.1).

rbiom 3.1.1

  • as_rbiom() and read_biom() now accept count matrices that are triangular, diagonal, or 1x1.
  • taxa_matrix() and taxa_table() no longer fail with “No taxa match the criteria” when taxa is a number and a sample has no abundance at the requested rank, e.g. with unc = "drop".

rbiom 3.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-05-08

  • Can now read and write biom objects from the biomformat package (microbiome/mia#818).
  • Fixed handling of objects from the TreeSummarizedExperiment package (microbiome/mia#822).

rbiom 3.0.1

  • Re-exports ecodive::list_metrics, ecodive::match_metric, and ggplot2::ggsave.

rbiom 3.0.0

Announcements

The code for rbiom’s very fast implementations of diversity metrics, rarefaction, and tree importing has been spun off into its own dependency-free package, ecodive, to encourage adoption by other R packages. This also means rbiom will be easier to install going forward as it will no longer need to be compiled.

Breaking Changes

  • weighted and normalized arguments are no longer used by any functions.
  • Diversity metric names will now be all lowercase in returned matrices, tables, etc.

The following functions have been deprecated since rbiom v2.0 and are now removed completely. They are generally functions which have been renamed for improved organization.

alpha.div, as.percent, beta.div, comments, comments<-, counts, counts<-, depth, depths_barplot, has.phylogeny, has.sequences, id, id<-, info, is.rarefied, metadata, metadata<-, nsamples, ntaxa, phylogeny, phylogeny<-, rarefy, read.biom, read_biom, read.fasta, read.tree, repair, sample.names, sample.names<-, sample_subset, sample.sums, sequences, sequences<-, subtree, taxa.means, taxa.names, taxa.names<-, taxa.ranks, taxa.ranks<-, taxa.rollup, taxa.sums, taxonomy, taxonomy<-, tips, top.taxa, top_taxa, unifrac, write.biom, write.fasta, write.tree, write.xlsx

Additions

  • adiv_vector() returns a simple named vector of alpha diversity values.
  • Replaced rhdf5 dependency with h5lite.
  • Updated list of alpha diversity metrics: c("ace", "berger", "brillouin", "chao1", "faith", "fisher", "simpson", "inv_simpson", "margalef", "mcintosh", "menhinick", "observed", "shannon", "squares")
  • Updated list of beta diversity metrics: c("aitchison", "bhattacharyya", "bray", "canberra", "chebyshev", "chord", "clark", "sorensen", "divergence", "euclidean", "generalized_unifrac", "gower", "hamming", "hellinger", "horn", "jaccard", "jensen", "jsd", "lorentzian", "manhattan", "matusita", "minkowski", "morisita", "motyka", "normalized_unifrac", "ochiai", "psym_chisq", "soergel", "squared_chisq", "squared_chord", "squared_euclidean", "topsoe", "unweighted_unifrac", "variance_adjusted_unifrac", "wave_hedges", "weighted_unifrac")
